integrations.purpose: Register a correspondence, mint its reference, issue one upload ticket per declared attachment.
Redeem one single-use ticket with the raw file.
Raise a helpdesk case. Never enters the registry.
Mail a one-time code to an address.
Exchange a code for a single-use proof.
Read one submission back, in the public projection only.
A verified citizen responds, adds a note, or withdraws. Appends to the timeline; only withdrawal changes status.
A fixed 60-minute window counter per endpoint per source. Read, then update or create, before the work.
One row per run, written inside the capture scope and never on the request path.
Mint a unique, monotonic reference per year. Replaces the last-three-digits-of-ticks scheme, which yields 1000 values a year and collides.
A receipt that a message was sent. Never the message body, and never a one-time code.

statuses.name: acknowledged
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than in_progress, blocked, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of in_progress, blocked.

statuses.name: action_complete
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from in_progress, awaiting_response through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than pending_review, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of pending_review.
statuses.entryGate: Response evidence is required: a response, a summary or a task id.

statuses.name: approved
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from pending_review, escalated through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than dispatch_pending, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of dispatch_pending.

statuses.name: approved_with_edit
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than dispatch_pending, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of dispatch_pending.

statuses.name: archived
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than reopen_requested, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of reopen_requested.

statuses.name: arrival
statuses.entryCondition: Not the target of any declared transition: this state can only be an origin.
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than registered, duplicate, rejected, on_hold, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of registered, duplicate, rejected, on_hold.

statuses.name: assigned
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from triage_complete, assigning through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than acknowledged, in_progress, reassign_requested, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of acknowledged, in_progress, reassign_requested.

statuses.name: assigning
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from triage_complete, assignment_failed through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than assigned, assignment_failed, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of assigned, assignment_failed.
statuses.reversalConditions: Reversible to assignment_failed: the map declares edges in both directions.

statuses.name: assignment_failed
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than assigning, triage_complete, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of assigning, triage_complete.
statuses.reversalConditions: Reversible to assigning: the map declares edges in both directions.

statuses.name: awaiting_response
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than in_progress, action_complete, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of in_progress, action_complete.
statuses.reversalConditions: Reversible to in_progress: the map declares edges in both directions.

statuses.name: blocked
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from acknowledged, in_progress through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than in_progress, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of in_progress.
statuses.reversalConditions: Reversible to in_progress: the map declares edges in both directions.

statuses.name: closed
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than archived, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of archived.
statuses.entryGate: The closure gate must pass, through the caller-supplied canClose() helper.

statuses.name: closure_check
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from no_dispatch, dispatched through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than closed, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of closed.

statuses.name: dispatch_failed
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than dispatch_pending, no_dispatch, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of dispatch_pending, no_dispatch.

statuses.name: dispatch_in_flight
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than dispatched, dispatch_failed, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of dispatched, dispatch_failed.

statuses.name: dispatch_pending
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from approved, approved_with_edit, dispatch_failed through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than dispatch_in_flight, no_dispatch, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of dispatch_in_flight, no_dispatch.

statuses.name: dispatched
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than closure_check, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of closure_check.

statuses.name: duplicate
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from arrival, registered through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Every transition out of this state.
statuses.exitCondition: None declared.

statuses.name: escalated
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than approved, returned, rejected, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of approved, returned, rejected.

statuses.name: in_progress
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from assigned, acknowledged, blocked, awaiting_response, returned through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than awaiting_response, action_complete, blocked, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of awaiting_response, action_complete, blocked.
statuses.reversalConditions: Reversible to awaiting_response, blocked: the map declares edges in both directions.

statuses.name: no_dispatch
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from dispatch_pending, dispatch_failed through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than closure_check, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of closure_check.

statuses.name: on_hold
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from arrival, registered through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Every transition out of this state.
statuses.exitCondition: None declared.

statuses.name: pending_review
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than approved, approved_with_edit, returned, escalated, rejected, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of approved, approved_with_edit, returned, escalated, rejected.
statuses.escalationConditions: Escalation is a declared successor of this state.

statuses.name: reassign_requested

transitions.evidenceNote: Declared edge of the internal-to-public status map.
The mapping is declared, and its own source records this particular edge as a reading rather than a fact, flagged for agency confirmation.
transitions.conflictingReading: "Accepted" means the registry accepted the item for handling, which is the public "Under review". If it instead means the request itself was granted, it maps to "approved".
transitions.conflictAuthorityAssessment: Both readings come from the same artifact, so neither is more current than the other and neither can settle the question. The artifact is authoritative for what the software DOES — it is the map the renderer calls — and is explicitly not authoritative for what the status MEANS to the agency, which it defers.
transitions.conflictImplementationRelevance: Implemented: the declared edge is what governedStatusLabel() returns today. A citizen is already being shown 'review' for a record the platform holds as 'Accepted'.
transitions.conflictValidationRequired: The registry owner states which reading is intended. If the alternative is intended, the map changes and, for the archived case, a distinct public state is needed.
transitions.validationStatus: Requires confirmation by the named owner

controls.name: Acknowledgement receipt
controls.description: Receipt of an assignment is confirmed and recorded before work starts.
controls.condition: The payload carries every required field, including an idempotency key.
controls.expectedBehaviour: A receipt is written to the ledger with actor, time, source and the idempotency key.
controls.outcome: A duplicate acknowledgement inside the dedupe window is recognised as the same receipt, not a second one.
controls.exception: A failed send is retried under the declared retry policy and queued when it cannot be delivered.
controls.idempotency: An idempotency key is required on every payload.
controls.evidenceNote: Enforcement, retry policy, dedupe window and receipt fields are all declared in configuration.

gaps.subject: Two artifacts authorise a governed action, and only one of them says what the action does
gaps.missingInformation: A per-action governance record for every name the runtime will accept, and a stated precedence between the two authorities.
gaps.availableEvidence: core/action-authority.js accepts an action when the per-action table carries a spec for it OR the module boundary charter lists it in owns[]. The table carries 65 specs, each naming an owner, a service, an audit vocabulary and a backend requirement. The charter declares 133 capability names across 34 modules, of which 89 have no per-action spec. The charter list mixes writes with view capabilities, so its entries cannot be read as actions without checking each one.
gaps.reasonRequired: An action authorised only by the charter runs with no declared service, no declared audit vocabulary and no declared backend requirement, while an action in the table runs with all four. Nothing states which authority governs when they disagree.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: Governed writes exist that this documentation can name but cannot describe: the FastTrack escalation and owner-notification actions are authorised by the charter alone and carry no audit vocabulary of their own.
gaps.operationalRisk: A write reaches the system of record without the audit event a reader of the governance table would expect it to write.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The platform technical owner, as the owner of both configurations.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Every name the runtime will accept as an action has a per-action record, or the charter states explicitly which of its entries are actions and which are views.

gaps.subject: Some governed writes cannot be named from their call site
gaps.missingInformation: The action name at the call site, for the modules that pass it as a variable.
gaps.availableEvidence: 4 module(s) — activities, executive, fasttrack, user-admin — call executeOwnedAction() with the action passed as a variable. Their actions are recovered from the per-action table and, where the name also appears as a literal in the module, from the boundary charter. Every recovered step is classified Inferred and says which recovery produced it.
gaps.reasonRequired: A step recovered by reading two artifacts together is weaker evidence than one read from a single call site, and the difference should not be invisible to a reader.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: For these modules, the mapping from a control the operator presses to the action it raises is a reading rather than a fact.
gaps.operationalRisk: An action could be raised that no artifact declares, and this documentation would not show it.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The module source, if the call sites are changed to name their actions literally.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Each call site names its action literally, or the module declares the set of names it dispatches.

gaps.subject: Internal status 'Accepted' maps to public 'review' on a reading, not a decision
gaps.missingInformation: An agency decision on what this internal status means to a citizen.
gaps.availableEvidence: The mapping is declared, and its own source records the ambiguity and the alternative reading: "Accepted" means the registry accepted the item for handling, which is the public "Under review". If it instead means the request itself was granted, it maps to "approved".
gaps.reasonRequired: A citizen reading the public label and an officer reading the internal one must be looking at the same thing.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: A citizen may be told a matter is at a stage the agency does not consider it to be at.
gaps.operationalRisk: Misinformed applicants, and complaints founded on a label the agency never intended.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The registry owner. The source itself names docs/audits/DESIGN_AUDIT_BRIEF_ASSESSMENT.md as the point of confirmation.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: The agency confirms the mapping, or supplies a distinct public state.

gaps.reasonRequired: A citizen reading the public label and an officer reading the internal one must be looking at the same thing.

gaps.subject: Two status models govern the same records
gaps.missingInformation: A stated relationship between the internal lifecycle states and the seven-state public vocabulary.
gaps.availableEvidence: Both models are declared in configuration. A mapping exists from five internal values to public ones; the lifecycle states are not among those five.
gaps.reasonRequired: A record moving through the lifecycle must carry a public status at every point, or the public surface shows a stale one.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: For most lifecycle states there is no evidenced public status.
gaps.operationalRisk: A citizen tracking a submission sees a status that does not move while the matter does.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The registry owner, with the platform technical owner.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Every lifecycle state carries a declared public status, or the two models are reconciled into one.

gaps.subject: Three status vocabularies govern the same records, and the widest one has no guard
gaps.missingInformation: A declared relationship between the lifecycle states and the stored status values, and a guard over the stored values.
gaps.availableEvidence: 31 lifecycle states in core/lifecycle.js, used by 4 core file(s); 6 stored values in modules/correspondence.js, carried in full or near-full by 3 workspace module(s) (approvals, correspondence, executive) and in single-value form by 9 more where the vocabulary cannot be established from the string; 7 public values. The declared internal-to-public map translates the STORED values, not the lifecycle states. The vocabularies share 1 name(s) (Archived) by coincidence of spelling, not by declaration.
gaps.reasonRequired: The lifecycle carries the transition guard and the entry preconditions. The vocabulary the operator surface actually uses carries neither, and nothing declares how a record in one is expressed in the other.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: The documented lifecycle controls do not demonstrably apply to the status an officer sets in the intake workspace, and a record moving through the lifecycle has no evidenced effect on what a citizen is shown.
gaps.operationalRisk: A governed transition can be bypassed by writing the stored value directly, and the two can disagree about the same record with nothing to detect it.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The process owner for the correspondence lifecycle, with the platform technical owner.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: One vocabulary governs, or each value in every vocabulary declares its counterpart in the others and a guard enforces it.

gaps.subject: The authoritative routing matrix is not among the supplied inputs; only the cascade fallback is
gaps.missingInformation: The reference data that supplies the live category-to-unit matrix, and confirmation of each mapping, priority and clock in it.
gaps.availableEvidence: 0 fallback rows, complete and machine-readable, under a key named fallbackMatrix, beside a declared list of the column names the live matrix may arrive under from reference data.
gaps.reasonRequired: Routing decides which directorate answers a citizen. It is an operating-model decision the software cannot make, and a fallback is by definition not the decision.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: Every routing rule documented here is a fallback. What the estate routes on when the reference data does supply a match is not documented at all, because that data is not present.
gaps.operationalRisk: Correspondence reaches the wrong unit and the service-level clock starts against the wrong owner.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The registry owner, with the SharePoint reference data the cascade reads its matrix from.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: The live matrix is supplied, catalogued row by row, and each mapping confirmed against the agency structure.

gaps.subject: Nothing fires an escalation when a service-level clock expires
gaps.missingInformation: An automatic trigger: a scheduled check, a flow, or a rule that raises the escalation when the acknowledgement or completion date passes.
gaps.availableEvidence: 0 routing rows carrying acknowledgement and completion day counts, which core/assignment-cascade.js turns into dated ack and due fields on the assignment. Breach IS detected — modules/fasttrack.js classifies every tracked item Breached, Due soon or Unassigned against its due date and reports the counts. Escalation IS available — governed actions raise an escalation level, force priority to urgent, write an escalation record, queue an owner notification, and resolve an open escalation. Every one of them requires an operator to press a control.
gaps.reasonRequired: The detection and the response both exist; only the connection between the clock and the response is missing. A clock whose expiry raises nothing is a measurement, not a control.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: A breach is visible only to someone who opens the FastTrack workspace and looks. Nothing reaches an owner who does not.
gaps.operationalRisk: Overdue matters accumulate unseen between visits to the workspace.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: A scheduled check or a flow raises the escalation and the notification when a clock expires, without waiting for an operator to open a screen.

gaps.operationalRisk: Non-compliance with the agency records schedule.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The agency records-management authority or its retention schedule.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Each class and period cites the instrument it derives from.

gaps.subject: Endpoint aliases are not joined to the workflows that answer them
gaps.missingInformation: A confirmed alias-to-workflow binding for every alias.
gaps.availableEvidence: 21 declared aliases, and a partial join covering some of them in docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/registers/portal-endpoint-workflow-ids.json.
gaps.reasonRequired: Without the binding, a documented client call cannot be traced to the documented workflow that serves it.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: The traceability chain breaks between the client step and the automated process.
gaps.operationalRisk: A change to a workflow cannot be assessed against the callers it would affect.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The tenant, through the runtime configuration that supplies each URL.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Every alias names the workflow id that answers it. Trigger URLs themselves must not be recorded: they carry a bearer token.

gaps.subject: A third role authority, derived from the email address and enforced by stylesheet
gaps.missingInformation: A statement of which authority governs, and an enforcement that does not rely on presentation.
gaps.availableEvidence: modules/executive.js derives DGCEO, Officer, EA from substrings of the signed-in email address, independently of the 6 roles and 4 personas in the access model. The panels each sees are separated by 5 stylesheet rule(s) using display:none.
gaps.reasonRequired: Three authorities decide what a person may do, and the one governing the executive decision panels is neither of the two the access model declares.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: The role matrix in this package describes route access. It does not describe who can reach the decision controls inside the executive workspace, which this variant governs instead.
gaps.operationalRisk: A display rule hides a control; it does not disable it. Anyone whose email does not match still receives the markup and the handlers.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The security or access authority, with the platform technical owner.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: The executive panels are gated by the declared role model, and the gate refuses the action rather than hiding the control.

gaps.subject: An authentication service is provisioned but is not evidenced as enforced
gaps.missingInformation: The deployed value of the authentication enable flag, and for each endpoint the trigger authentication type and any server-side role check.
gaps.availableEvidence: core/auth.js is complete and documents two postures. config/auth.config.js resolves the enable flag to false by default, and states the flag may also be injected at runtime from outside source. In the disabled posture the service returns the local profile as the identity and sends no Authorization header. canAccess() gates every route on a role and persona held in the client profile.
gaps.reasonRequired: A control enforced only where the caller controls the code is a usability feature, not a security control. Whether this estate is in that position depends on a runtime value these inputs do not carry.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: The access model documented here describes what the interface offers. Whether the estate refuses a caller who bypasses the interface is not established either way.
gaps.operationalRisk: If the flag is off in the deployed environment, direct calls to the endpoints are not subject to the documented role model.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The tenant owner, from the deployed runtime configuration and the flow trigger authentication settings.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: The deployed enable flag is stated, and for each endpoint the trigger authentication type and the server-side role check are recorded.

gaps.subject: No flow export states its business purpose, owner or criticality
gaps.missingInformation: Business purpose, process owner and criticality for every workflow in the estate.
gaps.availableEvidence: 36 complete action graphs, walked step by step. 0 of them carry a workflow-level description whose authorship cannot be established from an export; none carries an owner or a criticality field at any level.
gaps.reasonRequired: This standard requires purpose, owner and criticality for every process. A workflow export carries none of the three.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: No automated process can reach full documentation from confirmed evidence.
gaps.operationalRisk: An unowned workflow cannot be changed safely or retired deliberately.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The platform owner, from the tenant flow ownership records.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Each workflow names its owner, its purpose in one sentence, and its criticality.

gaps.subject: Test cases assert implementation invariants, not per-process acceptance criteria
gaps.missingInformation: For each process, what it is required to do to be accepted.
gaps.availableEvidence: 170 test files asserting invariants over the implementation.
gaps.reasonRequired: Without acceptance criteria, the implementation is the only definition of correct behaviour.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: A process cannot be judged correct or incorrect, only present or absent.
gaps.operationalRisk: A defect that is consistently implemented, and consistently tested, reads as intended behaviour.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The product owner, with the process owner for each area.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Each process names the criteria it must satisfy to be accepted, and a test asserts them.

Every action in every supplied export and paste package was walked and catalogued step by step. Business purpose, owner and criticality are unevidenced across the whole estate, so no automated process reaches full documentation from confirmed evidence.
Run records establish that the endpoints execute and what status each returns. They do not establish that any business transaction completed: none of the captured runs carries one.

A further 9 module(s) carry a single one of these values; a lone common word does not establish which status set it belongs to, and those are not counted as users.

terminology.definition: One node of a workflow definition. Every action names the actions it runs after and the status each must have reached.
A workspace that may raise a governed action it does not own. Ownership, service and audit vocabulary stay with the owner.
The routing matrix that derives responsible unit, assignee, priority and both service-level clocks from a correspondence category.
A scope whose run-after condition admits Failed, TimedOut or Skipped, so it runs when the scope before it did not succeed.
Departmental or service unit. The key by which the routing matrix names a responsible unit.
The name a module uses to reach a workflow. The URL behind it is supplied at runtime and never held in source.
A write that passes through executeOwnedAction(), which refuses it unless the calling module owns it or is a declared allowed invoker.
A workspace not on the sidebar, reached only from a named parent workspace.
One of the values in the frozen internal transition map. Distinct from the public status vocabulary.
One of the seven governed values a citizen is shown. Distinct from the internal lifecycle state.
The condition under which a Power Automate action runs, expressed as the predecessor actions and the statuses each must have reached.
A captured execution of a workflow: its outcome and the response it returned. Evidence of execution, not of business success.
A primary route on the sidebar, implemented by a module of the same name.

sources.reference: Reviewed as a whole: the suite asserts implementation invariants.

evidenceFramework.name: Confirmed
evidenceFramework.definition: A supplied artifact states this directly. Reading that artifact is sufficient to establish it.

evidenceFramework.name: Inferred
evidenceFramework.definition: Derived by reasoning across two or more artifacts. No single artifact states it.

evidenceFramework.name: Partially evidenced
evidenceFramework.definition: Some attributes are stated by an artifact and others are not. The record says which is which.

evidenceFramework.name: Conflicting
evidenceFramework.definition: Two artifacts disagree. Both readings are recorded; neither is silently preferred.

evidenceFramework.name: Unavailable
evidenceFramework.definition: The information is required by this standard and no supplied artifact carries it.

evidenceFramework.name: Not verifiable from the supplied inputs
evidenceFramework.definition: The artifact exists but does not permit the statement to be checked from the supplied inputs alone.

evidenceFramework.name: Requires authoritative validation
evidenceFramework.definition: Readable from an artifact, but the artifact is not authoritative for it. A named owner must confirm.
